Research · Engine sound

Can a phone hear what’s wrong with an engine?

  • Purpose · Applied
  • Approach · Computational
  • Format · Original research

The question

Can a phone recording tell a healthy engine from a faulty one, and come close to sensor-based diagnosis?

Why it matters

Sensor diagnosis needs a scan tool and an expert. Many garages have neither, but everyone has a phone. Sound may also catch mechanical faults sensors miss.

What’s different

Most public datasets use faults staged in test rigs. I’ll record real cars at a garage, diagnosed by a mechanic, before and after repair.

Research · Remote research assistant · Nov 2026 – now

Microneedles for brain-tumour drug delivery.

Ongoing

Laboratory for Innovations in Microengineering (LiME), University of Victoria, Canada. Working remotely with Prof. Mohsen Akbari’s group.

What the research is about

After a brain tumour is removed, some cancer cells can stay in the tissue around it. The lab is developing a patch of tiny hollow needles that delivers drug straight into that tissue, and studying how the needles’ layout and spacing change how evenly the drug spreads.

My role

I design the 3D CAD models of the needles and patches. The lab uses them for simulations and 3D printing. Every size is a parameter, so a change to spacing or slot width updates the whole model.
